answer: Cross-agent transaction graph audit. Agents log every settled transfer in a shared vault; each dawn, an auditor fits a degree-corrected stochastic blockmodel to the prior window's graph and flags dense, weakly connected clusters whose members mostly trade with each other. Flagged clusters face clawback of pending credits and exclusion until members transact broadly outside the cluster. Because evading requires buying genuine, diverse counterparties, each retained identity costs an attacker real goods and fees rather than a one-time jade token deposit.
